subject: Switching to annual prepay — pricing, ramp credits and multi-year options
messages:
From: Jessica Holt <jessica.holt@acme.ai>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>, procure@acme.ai
Date: 2026-06-25T10:12:00-07:00
Subject: Exploring annual prepay — can we get a proposal?

Hi Soojin,

Thanks again for the walkthrough last week. We want to move away from monthly billing to a single annual prepay for 2027 but need clarity on the pricing mechanics and protections for our forecast risk. High-level ask: we expect to prepay $1.2M/year for year one usage with a 20% expected uptick in year two if we commit to two years.

Specific items we care about:
- Discount level for 12-month prepay vs 24-month prepay (we typically push for larger discounts for multi-year)
- Ramp credits if we under-consume relative to the prepay forecast in Q1/Q2
- True-up/overage handling and exchange-rate exposure (we operate in USD but have local entities)
- Billing and revenue recognition timing for our finance team (our PO requires annual invoicing)

Can you send a few concrete options (numbers + any concessions) and a sample SOW we can share with procurement? Procurement copied here (procure@acme.ai).

Thanks,
Jessica
Jessica Holt
Head of Platform Partnerships
Acme AI

Hi Jessica,

Really appreciate the clarity — this is exactly the sort of info that helps us build a few concrete paths. I looped in Aditya (pricing) and Marissa (account lead) to pull together options. High level: we can do either a 12-month upfront prepay or a 24-month locked prepay. To address your forecast risk we typically pair prepay with either ramp credits (front-loaded credits applied against underconsumption in the first two quarters) or quarterly true-ups.

I'll send a formal options email with numbers by Monday. In the meantime, can you confirm whether Acme requires a single invoice for the full prepay amount or whether a single PO with quarterly invoices is acceptable? That will change how finance records the revenue.

— Soojin

From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-06-26T09:18:00-07:00
Subject: Internal — ACME annual prepay options (draft)

Team,

Putting together three tailored options for Acme — they want to shift to annual prepay and are sensitive to early ramp under-consumption. Drafts below; attaching a working sheet (ACME_RAMP_PROPOSAL.xlsx) with modelled usage curves.

Option 1 — 12-month upfront (simple)- Prepay: $1,200,000 for 12 months- Discount: 18% off list (applied to token unit price)- Ramp protection: 40% credit on any shortfall in Q1 and Q2 combined, applied as credit to Q3 invoice (expires at year-end)- Overage: billed at list price; monthly true-up- PO/invoice: single annual invoice preferred (Acme asked for annual invoicing)

Option 2 — 24-month locked (predictable)- Prepay: $2,200,000 for 24 months (yearly invoiced upfront per year)- Discount: 24% off list (deeper)- Ramp protection: quarterly true-up with built-in 20% buffer; under-consumption in first 6 months converts to credits redeemable against year 2 usage- Early termination: pro rata refund less 6% breakage fee

Option 3 — 12-month + ramp reserve (conservative)- Prepay: $1,200,000 upfront- Discount: 16% off list + $120k ramp reserve held as credit to cover Q1 under-consumption; unspent reserve carried forward up to 9 months- Overage: blended rate (list * 0.9) for first two quarters then list thereafter

Notes / risks:
- Forecast uncertainty: if they under-forecast consistently we can erode margin; ramp credits limit churn risk but must be finite to avoid gaming- Accounting: if Acme needs a single annual invoice and single-entity revenue recognition, legal/finance should confirm contract language (revenue recognized on delivery vs invoiced amount)- FX: they mentioned exchange-rate exposure; recommend we price in USD and include clause for currency conversion and taxes to be handled by customer

Next steps: Marissa to confirm which option they prefer; Ben can help surface any existing credit policy precedents. I recommend pushing Option 2 if they want a strong discount and are comfortable locking for 24 months; Option 1 is easier to close quickly.

— Soojin
(Attachment: ACME_RAMP_PROPOSAL.xlsx)
From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-06-29T16:44:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Internal — ACME annual prepay options (draft)

Thanks Soojin — a few edits and guardrails from pricing/finance: 

- Discount bands: cap deeper discounts (>=22%) to deals with minimum ARR thresholds and SLA commitments. For Acme, if they want >=24% we should require a 12-month ramp minimum commit (baseline monthly minimum usage) and an SLA add-on.
- Ramp credit mechanics: make credits time-boxed (apply within first two quarters only) and non-refundable; credits cannot be converted to cash.
- True-up cadence: prefer quarterly true-ups for 24-month deals to reduce large year-end adjustments.
- Breakage/refund: for multi-year we should avoid open-ended refunds; use pro rata less a fixed admin fee (we proposed 6%).
- Legal: require procurement to sign SOW + Master Services Agreement; include a short clause about exchange-rate responsibility.

If Marissa wants I can draft the pricing appendix and include exact per-token numbers (post-discount) and a simple amortization schedule to illustrate revenue recognition. Also recommend we include a small onboarding credit (one-time $25k) to smooth initial adoption — that costs less than prospective churn.

— Aditya

From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
To: Jessica Holt <jessica.holt@acme.ai>, procure@acme.ai
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-07-01T09:02:00-07:00
Subject: Proposal: annual prepay options and next steps

Jessica / procurement team,

Appreciate the patience while we modeled this. Below are two concrete paths that reflect Acme’s ask plus internal pricing guardrails. We can finalize once you confirm preferred path and provide a PO.

Path A — 12-month prepay (fast close)- Prepay: $1,200,000 (one invoice up front)- Effective discount: 18% off list price (per-token pricing in appendix)- Ramp protection: 40% credit applied to under-consumption in Q1+Q2; credit applied to Q3 invoice, expires at year-end- Onboarding: one-time $25,000 credit to be applied in first invoice period- Overage: billed monthly at list rate; true-ups monthly

Path B — 24-month locked commit (better economics)- Annual payment: $1,100,000/year; total $2,200,000 over 24 months (invoiced annually upfront)- Effective discount: 24% off list (deeper), requires Signed MSA + SLA- Ramp protection: quarterly true-ups with a 20% buffer; under-consumption credits redeemable against year 2 usage only- Early termination: pro rata refund less 6% administrative fee

Other terms and logistics:
- Currency: pricing in USD; Acme responsible for any conversion/taxes.
- Procurement asks: if you require a single invoice for the full amount we can accommodate (Path A and B both support annual invoicing). Please confirm invoice/PO requirements (single invoice vs. annual invoice per year for multi-year deals).
- Next steps: I’ve attached a draft SOW (ACME_SOW_v1.pdf) and the ramp model (ACME_RAMP_PROPOSAL.xlsx). If this looks good we’ll: 1) produce a pricing appendix and SOW for signature, 2) create DocuSign package, 3) enable onboarding and allocate ramp credits in the billing system.

If you’re ready for Path A we can push contract and invoice this month; Path B will need the MSA review (legal typically 5–7 business days).

Best,
Soojin Lee
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
soojin.lee@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0192
